newsitem.title: USA: U.S. clears Agouron's AIDS drug, stock soars.
newsitem.headline: U.S. clears Agouron's AIDS drug, stock soars.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc. said Friday the government has approved its HIV drug sooner than expected, prompting a sharp rise in its stock.

The stock rose as high as $96.25 before ending $4.75 higher at $80.50 on Nasdaq. It has been volatile since December as investors speculated when the Food and Drug Administration would approve the drug, called Viracept.

Approval was given under an accelerated process to market the drug simultaneously in formulations for adults and children. Agouron said it will be widely available at pharmacies throughout the United States next week.
The wholesale price of Viracept will be $15.48 a day or $5,650 for a 365-day supply at the recommended dose of 750 mg three times daily.
Viracept, which was developed by Agouron in collaboration with the pharmaceutical division of Japan Tobacco Inc., is a retroviral therapy for HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.

Agouron has established a patient assistance programme to help people in need pay for Viracept. It said it will provide the drug without charge to those patients whose need is greatest and who are least able to pay for the drug.
In addition, Agouron will provide Viracept without charge to any child in the United States who is not covered by public or private health insurance, the company said.

"It's extremely positive on the initial launch," said Jay Silverman, an analyst at Robertson, Stephens. "I do think they have a very competitive product, an experienced sales force, and a nice lead time over the next, nearest meaningful competitor," Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc., with Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
"It's extremely significant," agreed Robert LeBoyer, an analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman. "It's the product that been driving (the stock) since the $30 level."
Silverman said he expected the new drug to generate $30 million in revenues by the end of the year ending in June, and $165 million for fiscal 1998. He recommended buying the stock.
LeBoyer estimated that Viracept will generate revenues of $16 million for the fourth quarter and $150 million for fiscal 1998.
LeBoyer said he expects Agouron to lose $3 a share for 1997, and earn 30 cents a share for 1998. He has kept the long-term outperform rating.
Agouron reported a net loss of $12.6 million, or 93 cents a share, on revenues of $15.1 million in the second quarter ended Dec. 31.
LeBoyer said he expects Agouron's stock to hit $110 in 12 months.
